items.title: Funeral Program Template – Easy Fill‑In PDF for a Gentle Service
items.desc: Learn how to personalize and print a simple funeral program template. Step‑by‑step guide with printable sizes, editing tips, and printing options.
items.text: Planning guides How to Use a Funeral Program Template A funeral program template gives you a ready‑made layout that you can fill in on your phone or computer, then print at home or a local shop. It provides a comforting way to share the order of service, life story, and thank‑you notes with guests. What Does a Funeral Program Template Include? Our Soft Botanical suite provides a four‑panel program that folds to a 5.5 × 8.5 in booklet. The front cover welcomes guests, the inside panels hold the order of service, a short life story, and a thank‑you/reception note. All pages are formatted for standard US Letter paper (11 × 8.5 in) so you can print on any home or office printer. Cover – gentle botanical design with space for a photo and name Order of Service – timeline of the ceremony Life Story – brief biography or favorite memories Thank‑You/Reception – gratitude and reception details How to Personalize the Template on a Phone or Computer Open the PDF in the free Adobe Acrobat Reader app (available for iOS, Android, Windows, and macOS). Tap any sample text, type your information, and use the built‑in Save function. On a computer you can also add a photo by selecting the image placeholder and choosing a file from your hard drive. Download the PDF Open in Adobe Acrobat Reader Tap or click each text box and type Add a photo (computer only) Save the file Printing the Program at Home Print the saved PDF on 80‑100 lb cardstock for a sturdy booklet. Choose “Landscape” orientation, select “Fit to Page,” and print double‑sided if your printer supports it. After printing, fold the sheet in half to create the 5.5 × 8.5 in program. Use US Letter (8.5 × 11 in) paper Select cardstock for durability Print double‑sided, landscape Fold in half to form the booklet Printing at a Local Shop (Staples, Office Depot, FedEx) If you prefer a professional finish, bring the saved PDF file on a USB drive or email it to the store. Ask for the program printed on 100 lb cardstock, double‑sided, and cut to the exact size. Many shops can also mount the welcome sign on foam board for a polished entry display. Save PDF to USB or email Request 100 lb cardstock, double‑sided Ask for a clean cut to 5.5 × 8.5 in Mount the welcome sign on foam board (optional) When to Use the Full Soft Botanical Suite If you need a matching welcome sign (24 × 36 in) and share‑a‑memory cards (4.25 × 5.5 in), the Soft Botanical suite bundles everything for $12.99. The sign prints at the same 2:3 ratio, so you can also produce it at 16 × 24 in or 12 × 18 in without redesign. The memory cards let guests write short tributes that you can collect during the service. Welcome sign – prints at 24 × 36 in (or smaller) Share‑a‑memory cards – four per sheet All items share the same gentle botanical theme Questions Can I edit a funeral program template without paying for software? Yes. The PDF can be edited with the free Adobe Acrobat Reader app on any phone, tablet, or computer—no subscription or design program needed. What paper size should I use for the program? Print on standard US Letter (8.5 × 11 in) paper; after folding, the booklet measures 5.5 × 8.5 in. Do I need to print the program double‑sided? Double‑sided printing gives a professional look and saves paper, but you can also print one side, then manually flip and print the back if your printer lacks duplex capability. Can I add a photo to the program? Photos can be added on a computer by clicking the image placeholder in Adobe Reader. The mobile app does not support image insertion. How quickly can I have the program printed? If you print at home, it’s ready within minutes after saving. At a local print shop, most stores can finish the job the same day. items.title: Funeral Welcome Sign Template: What to Include, Sizes & Printing
items.desc: Create a gentle entrance for the service. Learn what to write on a funeral welcome sign, standard sizes, and how to print a matching template today.
items.text: Planning guides Funeral Welcome Sign Template: What to Include, Sizes & Printing A welcome sign sets a gentle tone as guests arrive. This guide covers what to write, which sizes work for easels or foam-board mounting, and how to personalize and print a matching template in minutes using free software. What is a funeral welcome sign and why use one? A funeral welcome sign sits at the entrance of the service venue — on an easel, a stand, or mounted on foam board — and greets attendees with the loved one's name, dates, and a short message. It helps guests feel oriented and welcomed before they take a seat. Unlike the folded program, which goes home with each person, the welcome sign stays at the venue. It works for traditional funerals, memorial services, and celebrations of life alike. Shows the full name, birth and passing dates Adds a brief phrase such as "Celebrating the Life of…" or "In Loving Memory" Matches the visual theme of the program and memory cards for a cohesive look What to write on a funeral welcome sign Keep the text short so it reads clearly from a few feet away. Include the essentials first, then add one personal line if space allows. Standard layout: full legal name (or the name they went by), birth year – passing year, service title ("Funeral Service," "Memorial Service," "Celebration of Life"), date and time of the service, and a short welcome line. "Welcome to the Celebration of Life for Maria Elena Rossi" "In Loving Memory of James T. Chen, 1952–2026" "Please join us in remembering Sarah — Service begins at 2:00 PM" Standard sizes and aspect ratios for printing Most print shops and home printers handle a few common poster sizes. The 2:3 aspect ratio (24×36 in, 16×24 in, 12×18 in) scales cleanly without cropping. A 24×36 in sign is large enough for a chapel entrance; 16×24 in fits a tabletop easel; 12×18 in works for a smaller foyer. If you design in a 2:3 ratio, you can print any of these three sizes from the same file — just choose the paper size at checkout. 24×36 in — full easel sign, visible across a lobby 16×24 in — mid-size, easy to transport 12×18 in — compact, fits a small stand or table How to personalize and print a welcome sign template Open the fill-in PDF in the free Adobe Acrobat Reader app on your phone, tablet, or computer. Tap each placeholder — name, dates, service title, time — and type your text. Save the file. No design software, account, or subscription is needed. Photos can be added on a computer only (drag and drop into the image frame). On a phone you can edit text but not insert images. Download the PDF instantly after purchase Open in Adobe Acrobat Reader (free, pre-installed on most devices) Tap sample text, type your details, save Print at home on heavyweight matte cardstock or send to Staples, Office Depot, or FedEx Office for same-day pickup Ask the shop to mount on foam board for rigidity on an easel Printing at home vs. a local print shop Home printing works if you have a printer that takes 11×17 in or 12×18 in paper and you're comfortable trimming. For 16×24 in or 24×36 in, a local shop is faster and cheaper than large-format inkjet ink. Most shops accept a PDF on a USB drive or emailed file and can mount on 3/16 in foam board while you wait. Call ahead to confirm same-day turnaround and foam-board mounting; some locations need a few hours during peak times. Home: 12×18 in on 65–80 lb matte cardstock, trim to size Shop: 16×24 in or 24×36 in on matte poster paper + foam board mount Bring the saved PDF on phone or USB; no account needed at the counter Matching the welcome sign to the rest of the service stationery A cohesive look — same fonts, colors, and botanical motif — helps the service feel intentional and calm. The Soft Botanical suite includes a folded funeral program (prints on US Letter, folds to 5.5×8.5 in), a welcome sign (24×36 in, also prints 16×24 or 12×18), and share-a-memory cards (4.25×5.5 in, four per letter sheet). All three are fill-in PDFs you edit in the same free app. When the welcome sign, program, and memory cards share the same design, guests experience a quiet continuity from the entrance to the seat to the memory table. One PDF kit — program, welcome sign, memory cards — edited in the same session Soft botanical greenery and neutral typography suit any venue Instant download, $12.99, no subscription Questions Can I edit the welcome sign on my phone? Yes. Open the PDF in the free Adobe Acrobat Reader app, tap the placeholder text, type your details, and save. Photo insertion works on a computer only. What paper weight should I use for a foam-board mounted sign? Ask the print shop for matte poster paper (typically 8–10 mil). They will spray-mount it to 3/16 in foam board so it stands rigid on an easel without curling. Does the template include bleed for edge-to-edge printing? The welcome sign file is set up at the exact trim size (24×36 in, 2:3 ratio). Most shops print with a small white border; if you need full bleed, ask them
